text:
In the Kumārasambhava

"May you obtain the unbroken love of your husband," the women said to Umā, who bowed low. But by her, who shared half the body of Him <note>referring to Shiva</note>, even the blessings of her affectionate kin were surpassed. (28)

Commentary: "Unbroken," meaning unblemished. Bowed, meaning humbled. Umā was addressed by the virtuous women, "May you obtain the unbroken love of your husband, Shiva." The use of the present tense with the particle *sma* denotes the past. Regarding him, the Destroyer <note>Shiva</note>. "Sharing half the body," refers to her state as half of his form. By her, Gauri <note>Umā</note>, even the blessings of her affectionate friends and family were surpassed, meaning they were rendered secondary, because the result she gained was far greater than what they had wished for.

The skilled mountain <note>Himālaya</note>, like a refined member of the assembly, having completed the duties of his daughter in a manner worthy of his desire and resources, remained in the gathering occupied by friends, awaiting the arrival of the Bull-bannered One <note>Shiva</note>. (29)

Commentary: "Skilled," meaning competent. "A member of the assembly," meaning one fit for a gathering. The mountain, Himālaya, having completed the tasks of his daughter Pārvatī according to his desires and his wealth, finished them completely. While in the assembly occupied by his friends, he remained, awaiting the coming of the Bull-bannered One, Shiva.

Meanwhile, upon the mountain of Kubera <note>Mount Kailāsa</note>, the mothers <note>the Seven Divine Mothers</note>, with great care, placed before the City-governor <note>Shiva</note> the adornments suitable for that former wedding. (30)

Commentary: "Meanwhile," means precisely at the time Pārvatī was being adorned. On Kubera's mountain, Kailāsa. The adornments, or materials for decoration, were suitable for that previous wedding. The mothers, such as Brāhmī and the others, performed this with great respect. They placed them before the City-governor, Shiva.

<summary>This passage describes the wedding preparations for Pārvatī and Shiva, highlighting the blessings given to the bride, the diligent involvement of her father Himālaya, and the divine preparations made by the Seven Mothers for the groom.</summary>
